name: prisma-database-setup
description: Prisma Database Setup Best Practices - Schema design, migrations, seeding, and environment configuration
author: prisma

rules.title: Use Prisma enums for fixed values
rules.description: Define enum types in schema.prisma for fields with fixed values (roles, statuses, priorities) instead of plain strings.

rules.title: Add unique constraints to natural keys
rules.description: Add @unique to fields that should be naturally unique (email, slug, etc.) to prevent duplicates at the database level.

rules.title: Add indexes to frequently queried fields
rules.description: Add @@index to fields used in WHERE, ORDER BY, or JOIN clauses to improve query performance.

rules.title: Consider soft deletes for audit trails
rules.description: Use deletedAt timestamp instead of hard deletes for entities that need audit history or recovery.

rules.title: Make seed scripts idempotent
rules.description: Use upsert with unique constraints in seed scripts so they can be run multiple times without duplicating data.

rules.title: Never commit .env with real credentials
rules.description: Use .env.example for template and .env.local for local development. Never commit production secrets to version control.

rules.title: Use descriptive migration names
rules.description: Name migrations descriptively (e.g., add_user_roles, create_tasks_table) instead of auto-generated timestamps.

rules.title: Explicitly define relation fields
rules.description: Always specify both sides of a relation with explicit field references and @relation attributes for clarity.
